lines.en: It’s as good a night as any to drown my sorrows in alcohol. And I’m sure Sara would agree as that is both her chosen method for doing the same thing and she’ll manage to make some money out of it.
However, now that her daughter has a newfound (or newly open) affinity for extracting semen from my body, there’s a good possibility I’ll be able to drown my sorrows in a different, cheaper way.
I’d probably pay if she really asked me to. But I’m glad she took after her mother’s thirst for teacher cock as I just happen to be a teacher who possesses one.
Anyway, beer.
Sex.
And orchestrated encounters with a small family of angels.
: Oh! Hey. I wasn’t expecting you to show up tonight.
: Neither...was I...
: Why? I come here all the time. What reason would you possibly have to believe that?
: I think we’ve just developed a Sensei-sense by now. A sense-ei, if you will.
: Can you...please stop making terrible puns? Even if this particular one is...mostly correct.
: Not if you want to stay in business, Sana. This building is quite literally built on top of a terrible pun.
: Well, yes— I am here. So your Sensei-sense is clearly lacking.
: Now, please provide me with ten beers so that I may drink myself into a stupor and ignore all of my other problems.
: No can do! I’ve got a job for you since you just so happened to wander in at the perfect moment.
: Are you...really going to make him come with you?...And just...leave me here on my own again?...
: Wouldn’t you be...better suited for that, don’t you think?...
: Nope! I trust you with my bar and my life, Sana. Plus, you’ve done it a million times before. And, if everything goes according to plan, you won’t have to start doing that again.
: I feel like I get dragged into “missions” more often than I’m supposed to here.
: Blame this one on Yuki, not me. She’s the one who keeps forgetting to show up for her shifts.
: Again? Really?
: She was...supposed to be here tonight, but...I guess she...forgot?...
: That excuse made sense last time. But if that keeps happening, something else is probably going on.
: Exactly. Which is why I’m headed over to her place now to make sure everything’s okay.
: And why you get to come with me so I’m not abducted in the middle of the night and sold into the sex trade!
: Alternatively, you could stay here and we could just...let her be abducted.
: Boooooo. Surely you don’t want me to be trafficked. Right, Sensei?
: Ten beers please, Sana.
: Coming right up, Sir.
: After all we’ve been through, you’re going to just let me become someone’s sex slave?!
: I’m not letting anything happen. I just can’t imagine the sex trade is going very strong right now on account of nearly every male being somewhere in space. This is a calculated, low-risk move.
: Sana, I would expect this from! But not you, Sensei!
: Okay, fine. I’ll come with you. But only because hearing that you’d expect your daughter to be okay with this is very sad.
: Yay! I’ll take what I can get.
: But what if someone barges in here with a gun and I get sold into-
: Actually, I’ll probably be fine. You two can go.
: Yay! You heard the girl! Come on, Sensei!
: Are you sure that’s a note you’re okay leaving on?
: Everything will be fine! You’re the most intimidating customer we get. So if you haven’t laid a finger on Sana yet, I doubt anyone else is going to.
: I repeat — are you sure that’s a note you’re okay leaving on?
: I don’t have much of a choice. For all we know, Yuki could be in greater danger than Sana is. And sending her out on her own is out of the question entirely. Bye, Sana!
: But...you could stay here and-
: Bye, Sana! Your mom is going on a date!
: No she’s not! But have fun! Take your time!
: If Yuki’s actually in trouble, do you really think we should be taking this so...lightly? She has ties to the Yakuza. That’s pretty serious, isn’t it?
: Oh, please. Have you seen Yuki? I’m pretty sure she could take the entire Yakuza out on her own. This is just a normal wellness check. I’m sure everything will be fine.
: Famous last words, Sara. Once you say that, you pretty much solidify that everything is going to not be fine.
: Well, then we need to go and figure that out! Bye, Sana! Date!
: Not a date! But still have fun!
: Date! Bye!
: Mom! Stop-
We’re outside now. I think we’re on a date.
Which, to be fair, I’m not really cool with. But it makes Sara happy and there are clearly bigger issues that need to be addressed right now.
I’m pretty sure it’s the kind that won’t end in sex, though. Especially since the entire purpose of it is to...make sure Yuki is still alive?
To be honest, I can’t help but worry. Because even though I’m not particularly close with Yuki, she has hollowed out some kind of spot in my mind or heart or wherever it is feelings come from.
: No answer again. I’ve called her like twenty times now.
: And...how many times has she missed work exactly?
: Four or five, I think. I haven’t exactly been keeping track. But I haven’t really needed to since business has started to slow down again.
: Any idea why?
: Not a clue, really. It feels like it just happened overnight or something. It’s fine, though. Chances are some new bar opened and people are just high on that right now.
: But that’s one more reason I have to figure out what’s going on with Yuki as soon as possible. We’ll need all hands on deck once the masses start returning.
: So this is purely a business venture we’re on right now?
: Of course it’s not purely a business venture. Yuki’s my friend. If she was just an employee, I probably would have only called her, like...five times.
: Have you brought this up at all to her? How did she explain her absence the first time? Or the times after that? Because there’s no way she’s just missed four or five shifts in a row, without-
: Sensei, I know you’re worried. I am too. I’m not just ignoring Yuki’s “history.” I know who she is and what she suffers from.
: But I’ve got it under control.
: Not wanting my little girl to be out in the dark alone isn’t the only reason I didn’t want her going over to Yuki’s place, you know.
: I’m prepared for the worst.
: And I’m sorry to drag you into it...but I’m way more comfortable with you by my side.
: Now, let’s get a move on.
: The quicker we get to her, the quicker we can rest.
I’ve been here before — with a smaller her.
And while their silhouettes are similar, there’s one inarguably closer to mine in more ways than one could count.
It’s better at matching my pace. And in between imperfectly timed steps, there’s no massive gap in size that would cause the laymen to question just how “it” would fit and how much it would hurt.
She’s older than me. She doesn’t know that yet, but it’s the truth. Yet, I’ve never seen her as an older sister.

There are things we have in common. Things that no one should. But it’s the type of connection that can only strengthen a bond when you want it to. At all other times, it’s the kind that should be feared.
Like two people witnessing a murder — locking eyes before heading their separate ways and forgetting they ever saw anything. Or at least trying to.
That’s the way it feels sometimes. Like we not only see each other, but we can see into each other’s pasts.
And I’m not sure how comfortable either one of us is about that. Especially when I’ve yet to divulge much of mine to her in any form.
Regardless, I can see her.
And in this light, despite it illuminating the path to somewhere much darker, she is beautiful as always while I step closer to the shadows to accentuate the difference.
A good friend is more apt of a description, I suppose. But despite how good she is, there’s this sort of...untapped or inaccessible knowledge that I want to grab hold of but can’t.
I’m sure there’s a life in which we’re closer. Maybe not as close as brother and sister, but close in a form where she would spread her legs or open her mouth with me upon command.
Would she drop to her knees right now if I uttered the required words? Or would she make me take her out to dinner first?
These are the bits of knowledge I’ve elected to forego in the name of protecting her offspring.
But I am certain-
There are much more important details in the fabric that are lost to my unclean eyes.
There are no words the rest of the way.
It appears I haven’t earned them.

But she will always be a side character.
And you will continue to crawl away from a world that’s breaking down behind you.
The pieces to your puzzle have fallen somewhere between the cracks. But you’re too scared to turn around and search for them.
And maybe you’re better off that way.
But maybe such a decision will make it possible to ever get out?
There’s only one way of knowing.
But there’s one more for someone stronger.

: So...it’s been a while since I’ve “checked in” on you.
: Probably on account of the whole coma thing. And the immeasurable sadness that has become my everyday life.
: Has your outlook on the world not changed since becoming a father?
: Did yours change when you became a mother?
: Of course. It’s pretty noticeable going from having no reason to live to having an extremely clear one. Was it not like that for you?
: Maybe it was years ago. I can’t...vividly remember that far back. But just changing what I call Ami hasn’t made as big of an impact on me as I thought it would at first.
: Hm.
: Guess I’m just a better parent than you, then.
: Guess so.
: The choice is always there for you to join my family, though. Maybe adding another daughter to the mix could shock you back into the initial thrills of fatherhood?
: Yeah, I’m not sure I could ever look at Sana as a daughter anymore. Sorry, Sara.
: Who says I’m talking about Sana? Maybe I’m suggesting that I want you to put a new baby in me?
: Wait- why wouldn’t you be able to look at Sana as a daughter, though? It’s not because she’s one of your students, is it? Because Ami-
: No, it’s not that. She’s just...
: She’s been...different lately.
: Different how? Because I told you to tell me if anything changed. If Sana is-
: I don’t...no. Not like that, Sara. I doubt she’s the same as us in regard to the whole “blacking out” phenomenon. But...she did mention having dreams.
: What...kind of dreams? Did she say? Because they could be important. They might...mean something? I don’t know. What were they? Do you know?
: I do. I just don’t know if it’s something you want to hear.
: I do. I need to know if it involves my daughter. Because she hasn’t said anything to me and-
: She’s been dreaming of something...someone you don’t like talking about.
: Yeah...But she started changing even before that.
: The thing is, though...I’m pretty sure it’s less of a change and more of her simply...revealing to me the way she’s always been.
: She’s kind of like a chameleon, if you think about it.
: She’s great at blending into her surroundings and making herself seem harmless. But she’s really an opportunistic hunter waiting for her chance to strike.
: Are you sure we’re talking about the same girl? Because my Sana isn’t like that at all.
: Then maybe she’s hiding who she really is from you too.
: Why...would she do that, though? I don’t get it.
: Beats me. People do all sorts of things that I don’t understand. And lately, Sana’s just...started to become one of them.
: I don’t like this.
: Just...part of being a parent, I guess.
: No, I don’t like that you’re hiding something from me about my daughter.
: You know how worried I am about her. You know how desperate I am to make sure she doesn’t wind up like me. I offered you my bar. My apartment. Anything you want...
: So is there just nothing you want? Or are you hiding whatever’s going on from me for some other reason? Be real with me, Sensei. As a parent. You’d want to know about Ami, wouldn’t you?
: Well...let me ask you this.
: If Sana did become like you — not in the sense of blacking out...or seeing things...but as a person — how would you feel about that?
: Hah...
: So that’s what you mean...
: I guess it really is in our genes then.
: ...Sara?
: When did it happen?
: When did...what happen?
: She came onto you, didn’t she? It was only a matter of time.
: Relax...I’m not mad. I was the same age as her when I went down that same path, remember?
: It’s not like I can tell her to “learn from my mistakes” or whatever when she quite literally only exists because of them.
: I regret nothing. And if this is what gets you to keep a closer eye on her, so be it.
: Sensei?
: Literally any response I make right now would either be incriminating or bad, so I’m just going to keep my mouth shut.
: It’s preferable to finding out she’s hallucinating and getting thrown on auto-pilot for hours at a time. At least I know she’d be safe with you.
: I’m an adult male. Your daughter is in high school and under five feet tall.
: I know. Isn’t she just adorable?
: Incriminate yourself already! I want to scold you for being a bad boy!
: I take it you’re just...fine with her becoming like you, then?
: Mm...I mean ideally, she’d wait a few more years until her body is fully developed to start fooling around with actual people. And even more ideally, she wouldn’t come after my boyfriend like this.
: I’m not your boyfriend.
: Yes you are. Shut up.
: I’m trying to. You’re the one who keeps trying to make me talk.
: Uhh, yeah. Because you totally just admitted that the reason my perfect future family’s in jeopardy is because my daughter is suddenly horny for her prospective daddy.
: Going back to silence now. Goodbye.
: If that is the worst of the changes you’ve seen from Sana, that’s like...the best case scenario. However, as her mother and your girlfriend, I can not give you my blessing.
: I don’t want your blessing. That’d be weird as hell.
: Great! That’s settled, then.
: What is settled? I have no idea where we even are in this conversation anymore.
: We’re at the part where I remind you to keep your eye on my daughter for actual developments or changes. Not ones everyone and their mother saw coming.
: Get it? Because I’m her mother.
: And I could tell she was hot for teacher just like me.
: Yeah, I get it.
: So you agree then?
: To...have sex with your daughter?
: Noooo! To tell me if and when something is wrong! I’m the one who gets to have sex with you! I worked for it! She can’t just swoop in and steal you! That’s not fair!
: Of course I’ll tell you if something’s wrong, Sara. But...I’d feel wrong if I didn’t make it abundantly clear that I might not know something like that.
: If Sana kept her feelings about me hidden for so long, who even knows what else she could be hiding? Revealing intimate details just...isn’t a thing she does?
: Then...what are we supposed to do?
: I don’t know...Wait and see if she tackles one of us to the ground and fucks us in the ass?
: Ugh! Again?! I can only take so much!
: Better you than me.
: Yeah because you’d get to stand there and watch while I’m sodomized and forced to figure out how to tell Sana she just screwed her own mom.
: You’d let me watch?
: Might as well. We’re already doing it.
: I’m going to have a lot of trouble figuring out if this makes you a better or worse mom when I’m getting into bed tonight.
: Aww, you think about me in bed? That’s so sweet! I do the same thing. Sana too, apparently.
: Sara...
: Boyfriend...
: How about we just...drop it? We’ll be at Yuki’s soon anyway.
: Works for me!
: You know, Yuki would probably let you screw her daughter too. She gets it.
: I don’t think either of you get it...
